findings.problem: The tag 'a real prime p: 617 digits' sits under the number '3231700607131100 ...', which are the leading digits of 2^2048 - 1. That number is not prime (it is divisible by 3), and a real 2048-bit prime would almost never start with the top-of-range digits of 2^2048. The scene (and its A8.same name 'a real prime') presents a composite as 'a real prime p'. The size claim (617 digits) is right; the label is not.
findings.fix: Relabel the tag to 'a number this size: 617 digits' (or 'p is about 3 x 10^616: 617 digits') and rename the assertion; keep the caption 'A 617-digit prime makes that search hopeless', which is true. Alternatively show only 'p: 617 digits' under a row of dots instead of the leading digits.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s4-14.7.png (tag 'a real prime p: 617 digits'); scene-04-numbers.js lines 51 and 238; node check: (2n**2048n - 1n) % 3n === 0n, and the lead digits 3231700607131100 are those of 2^2048 - 1.

findings.problem: Eve's hunt ends with a green hit at x = 6 but her 'a = ?' tag never resolves, so the hit has no consequence on screen. Lesson 8.3 (dhRun) says 'with p this tiny she finds a = t in t tries' and only then 'with a 2048-bit prime that search is impossible'. As drawn, a learner may think the 6-try search failed or did nothing, and the contrast with the 617-digit number is weaker. Green (valid/agreed) is also the colour of her success, with nothing saying 'toy broken'.
findings.fix: At 12.8-13.2, when x = 6 turns green, turn the dashed purple ghost 'a = ?' into a red solid 'a = 6' (D.a) with a small pop (so the toy secret visibly leaks), then the '617 digits' tag and the red 'no computer can search that' read as the contrast. Optionally recolour '6 tries' red-on-light or keep green but add the red 'a = 6'.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s4-12.2.png (five tries, 'a = ?' ghost) and algo-8-s4-14.7.png (x = 6 green, '6 tries', 'a = ?' still unresolved); lesson js/content/algo/algo-p8-x-02.js dhRun last frame.

findings.problem: Caption 8.2-10.8 'Recompute every later hash and it looks valid again.' runs ahead of its picture. The chain only looks valid again at 10.4-10.75 (last tick at 10.5, badge flips to 'valid chain' at 10.75, the caption's own end). From 8.2 to 10.75 the screen shows a red cross on link 2-3, block 3 red and the badge 'broken chain', so for about 2.5 s the caption states something that is not on screen yet.
findings.fix: Change the caption to describe the action: [8.2, 10.4, 'Recompute each later hash to repair every link.'] and leave [11.0, 12.4, 'Hashes spot edits. They do not stop them.'] as is; the badge flipping to 'valid chain' at 10.75 then supplies the 'looks valid' payoff on its own. (Or move the 'looks valid again' wording to a caption starting at 10.5.)
findings.evidence: algo-8-s8-9.0.png (caption 'it looks valid again', red cross, 'broken chain'), algo-8-s8-10.6.png (all ticks, badge still 'broken chain', caption unchanged), algo-8-s8-12.2.png (badge finally 'valid chain'); scene-08-chain.js header comment '10.75 valid chain again'.

findings.problem: Caption 8.8-11.0 'Each extra zero makes a hit 16 times rarer.' runs ahead of its picture. During the whole caption only the 16-cell strip and 'starts with 0: 1 in 16' are visible; the second zero ('starts with 00: 1 in 256') appears at 11.0, exactly when the caption ends, so the claim about the extra zero is never on screen while it is being said.
findings.fix: Re-time the two captions to the picture: [8.8, 10.9, 'One hash in 16 starts with 0.'] then [11.1, 13.2, 'Two zeros: 1 in 256. Each extra zero means 16 times more work.'] (replacing the current 8.8 and 11.2 captions), or bring the 00 tag forward to about 9.9 as the rows pop in.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s9-9.6.png and algo-8-s9-10.4.png (caption 'Each extra zero...', only the 1-in-16 tag), algo-8-s9-11.2.png (the 1-in-256 tag appears).

findings.problem: Caption 'Change one letter and every digit changes.' states as a rule what is only true of this example. For a good hash each hex digit stays the same with probability 1/16, so about 40% of one-letter edits leave at least one of 8 digits unchanged ((15/16)^8 = 0.60 that all 8 differ). Lesson 8.5 says 'a tiny change gives a totally different digest' and about half the bits flip (18 of 32 here), never 'every digit'. A learner will generalise the wrong rule.
findings.fix: Caption: 'Change one letter and the whole fingerprint changes.' Keep the orange tag 'all 8 digits differ' (true for cat and cot), perhaps as 'here all 8 digits differ'.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s7-6.9.png (caption), algo-8-s7-9.2.png (tag 'all 8 digits differ'); node check: A8.HASH.diffHex = [0..7], bits = 18 of 32; scene-07-hash.js lines 180-183.

findings.problem: Eve's red question mark beside her copy of XJHWJY says she cannot read a +5 shift cipher. Lesson 8.1 teaches the opposite for this cipher: it has only 25 keys, the 'Attacker's view' tries all 25 and 'classical ciphers fall to brute force'. A first-time learner can come away thinking a Caesar shift is secure and that the only weakness is key delivery. The video never says the shift is a stand-in for a strong cipher.
findings.fix: Mark the cipher as a toy: add a tiny grey tag 'toy cipher: real keys are huge' near the '+5' row, or extend the caption to 'A cipher scrambles it with a secret key (a toy shift here).' Keep the red '?' but tie it to 'without the key'.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s2-7.png ('+5' tags, blue XJHWJY, caption), scene-02-key-problem.js (Eve's qmark at 7.8); lesson js/content/algo/algo-p8-x-01.js a8-cipher takeaways and 'try all 25 keys' details.

findings.problem: The work bars (15 / 5 / 30 tries, total 50) have no baseline. Block 2 needed only 5 tries and block 3 30 purely by luck, so a first-time learner may read 'redoing the work' as cheap or as varying wildly. The lesson's expected cost is about 16 tries per zero (1 in 16), and the original sealing took 70 tries (28 + 25 + 17, A8.SEAL.totalOriginal), which is never shown, so 'all that work' has no 'that'.
findings.fix: Next to the '50 tries' sticker add a small grey line 'about 16 tries per block on average' (3 x 16 = 48), or show 'sealed the first time: 70 tries' above it, so the viewer sees that the rewrite costs as much as the original.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s10-9.4.png (bars 15 / 5 / 30 and '50 tries'); node check: sealed tries 28 / 25 / 17 = 70, forged 15 / 5 / 30 = 50.

findings.problem: The closing claim 'Rewriting history means redoing all that work.' omits the condition lesson 8.7 attaches to it: the attacker must redo the work while honest miners keep extending the real chain, and it is only safe while honest miners hold most of the power. Alone, the scene can suggest a forger who finishes the re-mining simply wins. The outline deliberately leaves the 51% attack out, so this is only a wording risk.
findings.fix: Caption: 'Rewriting history means redoing all that work, while others keep mining.' (or add 'while the real chain keeps growing').
findings.evidence: algo-8-s10-9.4.png (final caption); js/content/algo/algo-p8-x-04.js step 'Rewriting history needs most of the power'.

findings.problem: The fingerprints (8 hex digits) come from the lesson's toy 32-bit hash, but nothing on screen says so. Lesson 8.5 states 'This demo uses a toy 32-bit hash. Real systems use SHA-256.' A learner may believe real hashes are 8 hex digits, which also changes how they read 'starts with 0 = 1 in 16' in scenes 9 and 10 (a real network needs many more zeros).
findings.fix: Add a small grey tag, for example 'toy hash: 8 digits (real ones: 64)', under the middle machine or at the 8.8-9.8 hold; or add 'toy' to the machine label ('toy hash').
findings.evidence: algo-8-s7-9.2.png (machines labelled just 'hash'); no 'toy' string in any on-screen text (grep of videos/a8/scene-*.js).

findings.problem: Block 1's 'prev ecaf011a' is the hash of an unseen block 0 (the lesson's genesis block) and is never labelled, so a first-time learner meets an unexplained fingerprint at the very start of the chain and cannot tell where block 1's link goes. Scene 10 repeats it.
findings.fix: Add a tiny grey tag 'start of chain' (or 'genesis') above or beside block 1's prev row at 0.2-1.4, or draw a short stub link into block 1 from the left labelled 'start'.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s8-2.8.png (Block 1 prev ecaf011a with no incoming link); lesson js/content/algo/algo-p8-x-02.js chainRun (block 0 'genesis').

findings.problem: For about 0.6 s (4.4-5.0) the screen contradicts itself: block 1's card already shows its new hash 9a1f8189, while the check strip below still reads 'hash of block 1 = fb28ccb9' with a green tick and the badge says 'valid chain' (the strip only refreshes at 5.0-5.45). The label 'hash of block 1' is briefly false.
findings.fix: Start the strip refresh as soon as the hash roll ends (about 4.45), or fade the strip digits and the badge to neutral while block 1's hash is rolling (3.9-5.0).
findings.evidence: algo-8-s8-4.9.png (card 9a1f8189, strip fb28ccb9 with tick, 'valid chain'); scene-08-chain.js header timeline (3.9-4.4 hash rolls, 5.0-5.45 strip updates).

findings.problem: The headline 'Edit one block and every link after breaks' is stronger than the picture. Right after the edit only link 1-2 breaks; link 2-3 stays green with a tick until the forger patches block 2 (8.35). The lesson says the damage propagates forward when each repair changes the next hash, not that every later link breaks at once.
findings.fix: Headline: ['Edit one block and', 'the break spreads on'] or ['Edit one block:', 'the break ripples down'].
findings.evidence: algo-8-s8-6.5.png (red cross on link 1-2, green tick on link 2-3) versus the headline; lesson step 'Tampering shows downstream'.

findings.problem: Eve's four tries (55 / 2, 3, 4, 5) include 4, which is pointless after 2 failed. This matches the Attack button of lesson 8.4 ('divides n by 2, 3, 4 ... after 4 divisions') but not the lesson text: 8.2 says trial division goes 'one prime at a time' (2, 3, 5, 7, ...) and 8.4 says 'at most 15 trial divisions' for 2773, which counts primes only. The two lesson sources disagree and the video follows one of them without comment.
findings.fix: Either keep it (it agrees with the interactive Attack) or use the primes 2, 3, 5 and say 'in three tries'. If kept, make sure the lesson text and the video are reconciled when the lesson is next edited.
findings.evidence: algo-8-s6-10.0.png ('55 / 2', '55 / 3', '55 / 4' crossed, '55 / 5' ticked; caption 'in four tries'); js/content/algo/algo-p8-x-01.js (8.2 step 'Multiplying versus factoring') and algo-p8-x-02.js (atk handler and 'at most 15 trial divisions').

findings.problem: 'Blockchain' (and Bitcoin) appear only on the title card; scenes 8 to 10 never name the chain of hashed blocks 'a blockchain' or say proof of work is what Bitcoin miners do. Also the size tags say '617 digits' while the lessons say '2048+ bits' (lesson 8.4: 'real n has 2048 bits'), so the digit count is never connected to the lesson's figure. Both are small gaps between the title promise and the lessons.
findings.fix: Name it once: scene 8 caption 1 'Each block stores the hash of the one before it: a blockchain.' (or in scene 10's kicker). Put 'a real n: 2048 bits, 617 digits' in scene 6's tag (and 'p: 2048 bits' in scene 4) so the number matches the lesson.
findings.evidence: grep of on-screen strings in videos/a8/scene-02..11 finds no 'blockchain' or 'Bitcoin'; algo-8-s6-11.8.png ('a real n: 617 digits'); lesson a8-keys step 'Why this is only a toy' ('n has 2048+ bits').
